question: Which statement best describes Class syntax and the constructor?
options: `extends` makes one class inherit from another, linking their prototypes. In a subclass constructor you must call super(...) before using `this` — it runs the parent constructor. super.method() calls the parent's version of an overridden method.

Methods declared in the class body (without `function`) are placed on the class's prototype, so every instance shares one copy rather than each getting its own function. They access instance data through `this`.

Static methods and fields belong to the class itself, not to instances. They're called on the class (User.create()) and are useful for factory functions, utilities, and shared constants that don't depend on a particular instance.

A class declaration defines a blueprint. The special constructor method runs when you create an instance with `new`, receiving the arguments and initializing instance properties via `this`. A class can have at most one constructor; if you omit it, an empty one is supplied.
explanation: A class declaration defines a blueprint. The special constructor method runs when you create an instance with `new`, receiving the arguments and initializing instance properties via `this`. A class can have at most one constructor; if you omit it, an empty one is supplied.
